definitions.explanation: A black carbon material made by burning wood in a low-oxygen environment. Used for fuel, art, water purification, and deodorizing.

examples.japanese: {木炭|もくたん}で{火|ひ}を{起|お}こす。
examples.english: To start a fire with charcoal.

examples.japanese: {木炭|もくたん}デッサンの{授業|じゅぎょう}を{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I took a class in charcoal drawing.

examples.japanese: {備長炭|びんちょうたん}は{日本|にほん}を{代表|だいひょう}する{高品質|こうひんしつ}な{木炭|もくたん}だ。
examples.english: Binchotan is a high-quality charcoal representative of Japan.

notes: In everyday speech, {炭|すみ} is the more common word for charcoal. {木炭|もくたん} is the more formal/technical term that specifies wood-derived charcoal. Common collocations: {木炭|もくたん}{画|が} (charcoal drawing), {木炭|もくたん}{窯|がま} (charcoal kiln). The most famous Japanese charcoal is {備長炭|びんちょうたん}, made from ubame oak and prized for cooking and purification.
